chunks: And Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAmr ibn Saʿīd, from Muṣaddaq ibn Ṣadaqah, from ʿAmmār ibn Mūsā, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:

A man who forgot the tashahhud in the salat (prayer)—he said: if he remembers that he said only “Subḥāna Allāh,” then his salat (prayer) is valid; but if he does not remember having said anything of the tashahhud, he repeats the salat (prayer).

And he said: regarding a man who remembers, after he has stood up, spoken, and gone about his needs, that he had only prayed two rakʿahs of ẓuhr, ʿaṣr, ʿatamah, or maghrib—he said: he builds upon his salat (prayer) and completes it, even if he had reached China, and he does not repeat the salat (prayer).

So there is no contradiction between these two reports and what we have mentioned, because one who errs, gives salām, and then speaks afterward has not intentionally spoken during the salat (prayer); rather, he only speaks when he thinks that he has finished the salat (prayer). Thus, he takes the ruling of one who is in the salat (prayer) and spoke because he thought he was not in it.

But if, when he remembered that something from this salat (prayer) had been missed, he then spoke deliberately afterward, it would be obligatory for him to repeat the salat (prayer), in accordance with what we have already stated regarding deliberate speech.

However, we have already discussed the last report earlier and that it is not acted upon, because it conflicts with the principles. For the reports that are acted upon establish that if he has turned his back to the qiblah, restarting the salat (prayer) becomes obligatory upon him; rather, building upon it is only permissible if he remembers while still facing the qiblah. This report implies that even if he had reached China, he would not repeat the salat (prayer), and that is contrary to what we have stated.

key_terms.إِعَادَةُ الصَّلَاةِ: repeating the salat (prayer) from the beginning
key_terms.التَّشَهُّدَ: the testimony recited in the sitting of salat (prayer)
key_terms.سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ: a formula of glorification mentioned here as minimal remembrance
key_terms.يَبْنِي عَلَىٰ صَلَاتِهِ: he continues from where the salat (prayer) was left incomplete

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the tashahhud or speaks after mistakenly ending the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This passage discusses legal rulings concerning forgetfulness in salat (prayer), particularly omission of the tashahhud and speaking after mistakenly assuming the prayer had ended. It also distinguishes between unintentional speech due to forgetfulness and deliberate speech after remembering, while noting that one report is not acted upon because it conflicts with established principles regarding facing the qiblah.
